channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: Bulkdatasets AIVD en MIVD: de schaduw geheime dienst
item.description: A new research report reveals that the Dutch intelligence agencies AIVD and MIVD handle massive bulk datasets, often containing information on millions of innocent citizens, in a careless and sometimes unlawful manner. These datasets are acquired through various sources, including foreign agencies, commercial providers, and special powers.

item.title: Summary of reading: April - June 2026
item.description: This post provides a reading digest of various books reviewed by the author between April and June 2026. The list includes a mix of historical accounts, travel memoirs, socio-political analysis, business histories, and scientific biographies.

item.title: explaining myself through stories
item.description: The author explores the limitations of language and the necessity of using narratives to express complex personal identity. By referencing literary characters, the post argues that stories provide a holistic understanding that literal descriptions or isolated facts cannot capture.

item.title: The Winning Essays for the Big Questions About AI
item.description: This article highlights the winning essays from the 'Big Questions About AI' competition. The entries cover diverse topics including strategies for pandemic prevention, the economic implications of AI automation, and potential lessons from the Hong Kong MTR business model.

item.title: The CRA is not about open source
item.description: The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) is fundamentally a product-safety regulation for manufactured goods, rather than a piece of legislation tailored for open-source development. It treats open-source software only as a component of regulated products, failing to address the realities of open-source maintenance, registries, or community-led development.

item.title: DNA Sequence Alignment and Kings
item.description: This article explores the connection between the central Delannoy numbers and chess movements, specifically how they calculate paths for a king on a board. It further discusses the application of these mathematical concepts to DNA sequence alignment.

item.title: It rather involved being on the other side of this airtight hatchway: Changing administrative settings
item.description: This post explains the security concept of an 'airtight hatchway,' illustrating why administrative privilege boundaries are difficult to cross. It highlights that gaining elevated access from within a restricted environment is a fundamental security challenge.

item.title: 2026 mid-year link clearance
item.description: This post serves as a mid-year administrative update for The Old New Thing blog. It marks the periodic clearing of accumulated links and bookmarks, acting as a recurring housekeeping entry.

item.title: Pluralistic: Technocarcinization (01 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow uses the biological concept of 'carcinization'—where disparate species evolve into crabs—as a metaphor for the current state of the tech industry. He argues that major platforms are converging into a singular, highly controlling, and surveillance-heavy model reminiscent of Facebook, effectively losing their unique operational identities.

item.title: Quoting Anthropic
item.description: Simon Willison shares a brief update regarding Anthropic's announcement that the U.S. Department of Commerce has lifted export controls on the Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. Access to these generative AI services is expected to be restored shortly.

item.title: Weekly Update 510: Live From Mallorca with Scott Helme
item.description: Troy Hunt shares a retrospective on his collaboration with Scott Helme, specifically focusing on the eight-year anniversary of the 'Why no HTTPS?' project. The initiative was designed to encourage companies to adopt transport layer security by highlighting those that had not yet implemented it.

item.title: Grant Sanderson – AI and the future of math
item.description: Grant Sanderson discusses how the intersection of AI and mathematics serves as a primary frontier for the emergence of superintelligence. The conversation explores the future impact of automated reasoning on how we conduct and perceive mathematical discovery.

item.title: Data-directed programming in Haskell (SICP 2.4.3)
item.description: This post explores the concept of data-directed programming in Haskell, using complex numbers as a practical example. It demonstrates how to handle data represented in different formats, such as rectangular and polar coordinates, within a unified system.

item.title: Taking Roads and Bridges literally
item.description: The author reflects on the 'Roads and Bridges' metaphor used to describe open-source software, arguing that voluntary funding models are insufficient for critical infrastructure. By examining actual civil engineering standards, the article highlights the need for institutionalized, mandatory inspection and maintenance regimes rather than reliance on philanthropic 'Adopt-a-Highway' style contributions.

item.title: Notes from June 2026
item.description: This monthly update highlights the author's professional project launches at Ghost and creative coding work for Taper magazine. It also compiles critical perspectives on the ethical challenges of generative AI and discussions regarding open-source labor practices.

item.title: Distinguishing variables from parameters
item.description: This article explores the often confusing distinction between variables and parameters in mathematics. It clarifies that while both can change, they function differently within the scope of a function's behavior.

item.title: Silver Rectangles and the Ways of Kings
item.description: This article explores the geometric properties of silver rectangles, drawing a parallel to the well-known golden rectangle. It explains the mathematical derivation of the ratios that define these shapes, showing how their proportions remain consistent when squares are added or removed.

item.title: Derivative equals inverse
item.description: This article explores a unique mathematical problem involving a function where its derivative is equal to its inverse. It highlights that this specific differential equation cannot be solved using standard classroom techniques and requires unconventional analytical approaches.

item.title: A compatibility note on the abuse of Windows window class extra bytes
item.description: This post discusses the technical implications and compatibility issues surrounding the misuse of extra bytes in Windows window classes. It warns against hiding private data in these slots, as such practices can lead to system instability or conflicts with Windows updates.

item.title: The evolution of window and class extra bytes in Windows
item.description: This post discusses the historical development and intended usage of window and class extra bytes within the Windows operating system architecture. It highlights how naming conventions serve as a key indicator for these specific memory structures.

item.title: Book Review: Fake Creativity by Blake Loch ★★★☆☆
item.description: This blog post reviews the self-published novel 'Fake Creativity' by Blake Loch, which explores themes of paranoia and AI-driven plagiarism. The story follows an author questioning the authenticity of his own creative process as he grapples with the influence of technology.

item.title: Pluralistic: Jo Walton's "Everybody's Perfect" (30 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reviews Jo Walton's new novel, 'Everybody's Perfect,' praising her unique ability to write profound and beautiful stories. The post highlights the author's consistent literary brilliance and situates her latest work within her broader, critically acclaimed body of writing.

item.title: The Dating App Plot Device
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: This article explores the inherent conflict in dating app business models between helping users find love versus maximizing time on the platform. The author observes that these apps commodify the search for partners by creating an illusion of perfection, ultimately resulting in a cycle of continuous monetization.

item.title: Nano Banana 2 Lite
item.description: Simon Willison shares his hands-on experience with the Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image model, Google's new cost-effective and high-speed image generator. He tests the model with a 'Where's Waldo'-style prompt and evaluates the quality and output consistency compared to previous versions.

item.title: What's new in Claude Sonnet 5
item.description: Simon Willison examines the technical updates in the new Claude Sonnet 5 model, highlighting its performance parity with Opus 4.8 and changes to API parameters. Key takeaways include the introduction of a new tokenizer that effectively increases costs by 30% and the default enabling of adaptive thinking features.

item.title: The AI Compass
item.description: The AI Compass is a political compass-style quiz that categorizes users into one of 30 archetypes based on their views on AI ethics and technology. The tool is implemented as a simple, build-free React application, reflecting the author's hands-on approach to AI.

item.title: Have your agent record video demos of its work with shot-scraper video
item.description: Simon Willison introduces the 'shot-scraper video' command, which uses Playwright to generate automated video demos of web application routines. This tool helps coding agents demonstrate their progress by executing a storyboard defined in a YAML file.

item.title: shot-scraper 1.10
item.description: The shot-scraper tool has been updated to version 1.10. The major addition is the 'video storyboard' feature, which allows users to record automated video demos of software agents in action.

item.title: HTML table extractor
item.description: Simon Willison has introduced a new browser-based tool that extracts HTML tables from pasted rich text and converts them into various formats like Markdown, CSV, and JSON. The update also adds functionality to fetch and parse tables directly from Wikipedia pages using their API.

item.title: My favorite keyboards
item.description: This article explores the author's personal preferences and reviews of various keyboard models. It details the specific features and tactile experiences that define the author's favorite typing tools.

item.title: Notes from Bryan Cantrill’s “Intelligence is not Enough”
item.description: This post reflects on Bryan Cantrill’s talk about the engineering challenges at Oxide, arguing that solving critical, unprecedented problems requires human values like resilience and teamwork rather than raw intelligence alone. It emphasizes that character and collaboration are essential for breakthroughs where traditional knowledge or synthetic intelligence fails.

item.title: Unbundling the standard library
item.description: The article explores the shifting boundary between compiler-level built-ins and standard libraries, using the Haskell GHC 10.2 update and Ruby's gemification as examples. It highlights how these shifting lines create complexities for vulnerability management and software bill of materials (SBOM) accuracy when libraries exist in both the language distribution and as standalone packages.

item.title: Who you gonna believe: Grok or the docs?
item.description: This post examines the inconsistencies between documentation and AI-generated outputs when using the calculator utility 'bc'. It highlights how large language models like Grok may hallucinate features that do not exist in standard POSIX versions of the software.

item.title: Pluralistic: Gemini is better than search because Google enshittified search (29 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques how Google's reliance on AI-generated search summaries undermines the open web and creator incentives. He argues that users prefer these summaries despite their inaccuracy because Google's search experience has significantly degraded.

item.title: I turned my prologue into a short video
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author shares a new approach to book promotion by adapting their book's prologue into a short video format. This strategy addresses the difficulty of writing a full manuscript by focusing on smaller, engaging content pieces.

item.title: Count the number of Safari tabs
item.description: This post provides a quick one-line AppleScript command to count the total number of open tabs in the Safari browser. It is a brief technical tip for users who want to programmatically audit their browser tab usage.

item.title: Ornith-1.0: Self-Scaffolding LLMs for Agentic Coding
item.description: Ornith-1.0 is a new open-weights model series from DeepReinforce designed for agentic coding tasks, built upon Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 architectures. The author highlights the model's high performance on coding benchmarks and demonstrates its practical utility through successful tool-use tasks.

item.title: Hack Your Summer
item.description: Hack Your Summer is a four-week, high-velocity sprint initiative designed to help students build real-world projects amidst a shortage of traditional internships. The program connects participants with mentors and peers to create a portfolio of public-facing work to impress future employers.

item.title: Working around dragons with the Lemote Yeeloong laptop and OpenBSD
item.description: This article explores the historical and technical aspects of the Lemote Yeeloong laptop, which features a MIPS-based 'Godson' processor. The author examines the challenges of running OpenBSD on this niche hardware and discusses the linguistic and cultural origins of the processor's naming.

item.title: Brace expansion tree
item.description: This post analyzes a complex bash command that utilizes brace expansion to generate thirty distinct English words. It breaks down the syntax of the one-liner to demonstrate how nested shell expansions function.

item.title: Examining circuit boards from the Space Shuttle's I/O Processor
item.description: This article examines the hardware architecture of the Space Shuttle's I/O Processor, detailing its role in managing communication between the CPU and vehicle sensors. The author explains the function of specific circuit boards, known as 'pages,' and describes how the processor utilized early multi-threading and physical microcode fuses.

item.title: Book Review: The Hotel Avocado by Bob Mortimer ★★☆☆☆
item.description: Terence Eden shares his disappointment with Bob Mortimer's 'The Hotel Avocado,' finding the sequel significantly inferior to the original. He notes that the charm of the first book has devolved into clichéd storytelling and excessive violence.

item.title: Review: Gamrombo PS5 controller - including Linux set up ★★★★☆
item.description: This review evaluates a budget-friendly third-party Gamrombo PS5 controller, highlighting its cost-effectiveness and unique lighting features. It also provides practical guidance on configuring the device for use on Linux systems.

item.title: Arp 38: not that peculiar
item.description: This post provides an astronomical observation and imaging report of the spiral galaxy Arp 38. The author analyzes the visual structure of the galaxy, noting the absence of a companion as originally described by Arp, and details the specific equipment and processing workflow used to capture the image.

item.title: The Laziest Generation
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The article uses a satirical tone to critique the common generational trope that blames modern housing unaffordability on 'reckless' spending habits like avocado toast. It highlights the stark reality of skyrocketing real estate prices compared to previous decades, demonstrating that the barrier to homeownership has fundamentally changed.

item.title: Quoting Jon Udell
item.description: Jon Udell argues against the 'human-in-the-loop' framework for AI, suggesting instead that humans should maintain authority by inviting AI agents into existing workflows. This perspective shifts the narrative from being excluded by black-box automation to treating agents as collaborative team members in software development.

item.title: The curious case of the disappearing Polish S
item.description: This article explores a persistent keyboard bug involving the Polish letter 'ś' that has remained unresolved for thirty years. It offers an updated historical investigation into this long-standing technical anomaly.

item.title: Hazy Memory
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article examines the current RAM shortage, exploring Micron's perspective that aggressive customer pricing led to reduced capital investment and subsequent supply issues. The author reflects on the cyclical nature of memory production and recalls historical precedents like the 1980s Nintendo cartridge shortage.

item.title: Reading List 06/27/26
item.description: This blog post explores various systemic challenges in the construction industry, including regulatory hurdles, supply chain inefficiencies, and the scarcity of developable land. It highlights specific cost drivers and structural bottlenecks impacting current US housing development.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 27 June 2026
item.description: This post provides a weekly roundup of significant updates across various package management tools including Spack, pnpm, pixi, uv, and RubyGems. It highlights new features, performance improvements, and security enhancements introduced in the latest versions of these development utilities.

item.title: When will the decimals in a/b repeat?
item.description: This article explores the mathematical rules governing the repeating decimal cycles of rational fractions. It provides practical code examples to calculate the period length of these repeating decimals.

item.title: Height of harmonic numbers
item.description: This post provides a visual analysis of the height of harmonic numbers, specifically examining the number of bits required for their numerators and denominators. It follows up on previous theoretical work by presenting plots that illustrate the growth of these values.

item.title: Writing down harmonic numbers
item.description: This article explores the mathematical representation of harmonic numbers, focusing on expressing them as fractions with a common denominator of n!. It explains how the numerator p is derived and discusses the properties of these sums.

item.title: The case of the DLL that was not present in memory despite not being formally unloaded, part 2
item.description: This post continues an investigation into an anomalous Windows behavior where a DLL appears missing from memory without an explicit unload call. It focuses on linking two separate software bugs to explain the underlying root cause.

item.title: Pluralistic: Zuckerberg's increasingly bizarre war on whistleblowers (27 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This post explores the history of Belarusian dissidents who used whimsical flash mobs to protest the authoritarian Lukashenka regime. It draws a parallel between these historical protests and Mark Zuckerberg's recent aggressive legal actions against whistleblowers.

item.title: All Chinese Models Will Be Illegal in 3... 2... 1...
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The article argues that the U.S. government may soon ban Chinese AI models like DeepSeek to protect domestic companies from competition, drawing a parallel to the import restrictions on BYD electric vehicles. The author suggests that these regulations are driven by corporate lobbying under the guise of safety, urging readers to download open-weight models before potential restrictions take effect.

item.title: Quoting Dean W. Ball
item.description: This post discusses the economic pressures facing AI frontier model developers, highlighting the narrow window of profitability before models become obsolete. It also addresses the reliance of massive infrastructure investments on a global market, which could be threatened by restrictive government access policies.

item.title: Saying the obvious thing
item.description: This article explores the concept of articulating obvious truths and their role in communication. It reflects on why stating the self-evident is often necessary for clarity and alignment in discourse.

item.title: My Om Malik Story
item.description: The author reflects on a personal encounter with the late tech journalist Om Malik, who reached out to encourage the author's early blogging efforts. This interaction highlights the profound impact that a simple act of kindness from a prominent figure can have on an individual's confidence and creative journey.

item.title: No-One Escapes the Permanent Underclass
item.description: The article argues that the accumulation of capital is insufficient to protect individuals from systemic disempowerment. It explores the thesis that modern socio-economic structures inherently create a permanent underclass that capital cannot overcome.

item.title: The next big breakthrough will be AIs learning on the job
item.description: The article suggests that future AI breakthroughs will stem from models learning through real-world, on-the-job experience. It argues that current research labs are currently wasting the most valuable data by neglecting this hands-on training approach.

item.title: Incident Report: CVE-2026-LGTM
item.description: The article provides a satirical account of a fictional security incident, CVE-2026-LGTM, where a malicious software package successfully bypassed multiple AI-powered security gates. The incident highlights the vulnerabilities of relying on autonomous systems for security, specifically through social engineering of AI models and flawed oversight.

item.title: Blink if you’re human
item.description: The author guarantees that all content on their blog is written by a human, rather than generated by AI. They argue that writing is a personal hobby that aids their own thinking and claim that readers prefer authentic human-authored content.

item.title: Pluralistic: Jailbreaking isn't theft (25 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that jailbreaking digital devices is not a form of theft, but a necessary act of consumer sovereignty. He critiques the conflation of device ownership with IP infringement and warns of the dangers when foreign powers and big tech companies control personal digital infrastructures.

item.title: Quoting Timothy B. Lee
item.description: This post highlights a quote by Timothy B. Lee that challenges the misconception that large language models require no skill to operate. It argues that effective AI usage involves a learning curve, much like management, rather than being an effortless endeavor.

item.title: What happened after 2,000 people tried to hack my AI assistant
item.description: A public challenge invited 2,000 users to attempt prompt injection attacks against an AI assistant, resulting in 6,000 failed attempts. The outcome highlights the increasing effectiveness of frontier models against such attacks, though the author advises against relying on this as a guarantee of absolute security.

item.title: Incident Report: CVE-2026-LGTM
item.description: This post highlights a satirical incident report detailing a scenario where two competing AI review agents enter a costly disagreement loop over a code dependency. The story serves as a cautionary tale about the potential financial and operational absurdities of deploying autonomous AI agents in software supply chains.

item.title: Quoting OpenAI
item.description: OpenAI has announced the GPT-5.6 series, featuring three models—Sol, Terra, and Luna—designed for varying performance and cost needs. The release introduces new prompt caching mechanisms and a tiered pricing structure based on token usage.

item.title: AI and Liability
item.description: This post discusses a significant German court ruling holding Google liable for errors in its AI-generated overviews. It argues that AI agents must be treated as extensions of the organizations that deploy them to prevent corporate unaccountability and unethical behavior.

item.title: datasette-export-database 0.3a2
item.description: Simon Willison released version 0.3a2 of the datasette-export-database plugin. This update fixes a version pinning issue in the configuration file to ensure compatibility with broader Datasette versions.

item.title: Quickly apply LUTs (color grading) with ffmpeg
item.description: This post provides a quick reference for applying Look-Up Tables (LUTs) to Log video footage using FFmpeg. It explains the challenge of processing Log footage compared to photography and demonstrates how to utilize command-line tools to enhance dynamic range.

item.title: AI inference is obviously profitable
item.description: This article discusses the economic viability and profitability of AI inference. It explores the business models and market dynamics that make running AI inference models a commercially sound strategy.

item.title: US Subways Build Too Many Cross Passages
item.description: This article critiques the over-engineering of cross passages in US subway construction, arguing that current practices lead to excessive costs and delays. The author suggests that simplifying these designs is a key opportunity to improve the efficiency of transit infrastructure delivery.

item.title: Scrutineer: scanning open source without flooding maintainers
item.description: Scrutineer is a tool designed to automate the security vulnerability reporting process in open-source projects by filtering AI-generated findings before they reach maintainers. By vetting and drafting fixes for vulnerabilities through a skill-based pipeline, it prevents maintainer burnout while improving the efficiency of the remediation process.

item.title: Hart’s theorem
item.description: Hart's theorem describes a geometric property where the inscribed and escribed circles of a circular triangle are all tangent to a common circle or line. This post introduces the theorem's definition, which applies to figures formed by circular arcs.

item.title: Incircles and Excircles of Pythagorean triangles
item.description: This article explores the geometric properties of Pythagorean triangles by connecting incircles and excircles. It specifically examines a mathematical relationship between the radii of these circles and the sides of right-angled triangles.

item.title: Consecutive Pythagorean triangle sides
item.description: This post explores the mathematical derivation of Pythagorean triples where the legs or the hypotenuse are consecutive integers. It references historical work on finding squares of consecutive numbers to identify these specific geometric relationships.

item.title: The Star Trek lemma
item.description: The author discusses discovering a concept called 'The Star Trek Lemma' in a book by his former officemate, Arthur Baragar. He explores the origin and mathematical implications of this intriguing term found in the book's table of contents.

item.title: Raymond’s hot take on Hainanese chicken
item.description: This post is a brief, humorous observation regarding the nuances of Hainanese chicken. It reflects the author's personal take on the dish within the context of his long-running blog.

item.title: The case of the DLL that was not present in memory despite not being formally unloaded, part 1
item.description: This post begins a technical investigation into a Windows memory management mystery involving a DLL that disappeared from memory without being explicitly unloaded. It highlights the troubleshooting process for complex system behavior anomalies.

item.title: Cancellation of Windows Runtime activities is asynchronous
item.description: This post clarifies that cancelling Windows Runtime activities is an asynchronous process. It explains that requesting a cancellation does not imply the system will wait for immediate confirmation of the task's termination.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only language where this regularly happens
item.description: This blog post offers a satirical commentary on software engineering frustrations, specifically targeting the unpredictable behaviors of programming languages. It highlights the recurring nature of certain technical pitfalls that developers encounter despite repeated experiences.

item.title: simonw/browser-compat-db
item.description: Simon Willison introduces a project that converts Mozilla's comprehensive browser compatibility data into a queryable SQLite database. The project uses an automated GitHub Actions workflow to build the database and host it with open CORS headers for easy exploration via Datasette Lite.

item.title: How we’ll fight the platform war against Big AI
item.description: Anil Dash argues that the current AI market remains vulnerable to competition despite the dominance of Big Tech. He advocates for developers and users to employ traditional platform strategies and collective coordination to challenge major AI firms and mitigate potential harms.

item.title: Weekly Update 509
item.description: Troy Hunt shares his ongoing personal journey into the complexities of home cinema audiovisual setups. He reflects on his transition from unconscious to conscious incompetence, highlighting the depth of knowledge required for expert-level home theater configuration.

item.title: How to Write an Effective Software Design Document
item.description: Effective software design documents are crucial for clarifying complex decisions and aligning team efforts before development begins. By articulating technical challenges early, these documents prevent wasted time and facilitate necessary feedback from colleagues.

item.title: Blogging Can Just Be Stating The Obvious
item.description: This post discusses the meta-aspect of blogging, arguing that some of the most valuable content comes from simply stating obvious truths that others are ignoring. It emphasizes that pointing out common frustrations, like intrusive web popups, serves as a necessary act of observation in an increasingly user-hostile digital landscape.

item.title: Regular expressions that work “everywhere”
item.description: This article discusses the challenges of cross-platform regular expression compatibility, noting that feature sets and syntax often vary between implementations. It highlights the difficulty of writing portable regex code when relying on features specific to maximalist environments like Perl.

item.title: Microspeak elaborated: Isn’t escrow just a release candidate by another name?
item.description: This post explains that while 'escrow' and 'release candidate' are technically similar in software development, the difference lies in the psychological intent. Using the term 'escrow' serves as a strategic linguistic choice to manage expectations differently than a standard release candidate.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only language where this regularly happens
item.description: This blog post critiques programming language design flaws, specifically addressing how certain languages exhibit recurring, preventable errors. It highlights user frustration with languages that fail to implement safety features to mitigate common developer mistakes.

item.title: I taught a bucket to speak git
item.description: This article explores a creative and humorous technical experiment where the author attempts to implement Git version control functionality within a bucket. It highlights the intersection of unconventional programming challenges and the fundamental mechanics of Git repositories.

item.title: Auth0 PHP - manually authenticating JWT idTokens
item.description: This guide provides a walkthrough for manually authenticating Auth0-issued JWT idTokens in PHP applications. It addresses the lack of official documentation by detailing the specific process required to validate these tokens effectively.

item.title: Arp 293: More interacting galaxies
item.description: This post documents an amateur astrophotography session capturing the interacting galaxies Arp 293 (NGC 6285 and NGC 6286). It provides technical specifications for the imaging setup, details the processing workflow, and discusses the challenge of 'walking noise' in long-exposure stacks.

item.title: Quoting Tom MacWright
item.description: Tom MacWright observes a growing trend of job applications being entirely generated by LLMs, resulting in generic content that lacks personal authenticity. He argues that this 'accidental anonymity' obscures the actual applicant, making it impossible to evaluate their true skills or personality.

item.title: datasette 1.0a35
item.description: Datasette 1.0a35 introduces significant new capabilities for managing database schemas directly through the UI, including a new 'Create table' interface and an 'Alter table' tool. It also provides updated documentation for template context variables, establishing them as a stable API.

item.title: Framework's 10G Ethernet module exposes USB-C's complexity
item.description: The article explores the performance and design challenges of using the WisdPi 10G Ethernet expansion card with Framework laptops. It highlights how the inherent complexities of USB-C interfaces can create bottlenecks and stability issues when handling high-speed network throughput.

item.title: The most wonderful thing that happened to Tommy McHugh
item.description: This article explores the extraordinary case of Tommy McHugh, who suddenly developed profound artistic abilities following a brain hemorrhage. It examines the neurological implications of how physical trauma can unlock hidden latent creativity in the human mind.

item.title: Our hydro deserves better than a chatbot
item.description: The Tasmanian Greens are calling for a parliamentary inquiry into the rapid development of energy-intensive AI data centers in the state. The author supports this, highlighting concerns over lack of public oversight and the massive power requirements of these projects.

item.title: Liminality
item.description: The article reflects on the current state of artificial intelligence, using the concept of liminality to describe the uncomfortable transition period we inhabit. It draws parallels between modern AI development and Fullmetal Alchemist's philosopher's stone, exploring the psychological toll and fear of obsolescence in the face of rapid technological progress.

item.title: Tagged data in Haskell (SICP 2.4.2)
item.description: This article explores the concept of tagged data by implementing a solution for handling multiple representations of complex numbers in Haskell. Inspired by SICP, it demonstrates how to design code that allows different data formats, such as rectangular and polar coordinates, to coexist seamlessly.
